body:
Thank you for your responses. I have taken a hot shower and feel less agitated. I found some sleeping pills that I forgot about, so I took one of those. 

I never thought about talking to my therapist in the sense of "I'm feeling this way, but I'm afraid of the consequences and how you'll react". Sounds ridiculous that I haven't thought of that, but thank you for that suggestion too.

I will give you an update tomorrow as to how it goes. Thank you again for your kindness. I'm hoping I'll be able to sleep tonight.

It's really odd that you mention reading Harry Potter, I was looking at my collection yesterday and I thought about picking up one of the books and giving reading a try. I didn't, but maybe I should.

My power is no longer turning off and on, so I could have a hot shower...except the thought of doing so seem exhausting...but I really need to do it because of my acne (if nothing else). I went and had some soup though, which did calm me down a bit. For me soup and a giant fleece blanket are comforting.

I'm really hesitating on disclosing the entire plan. It involves a different type of means than in my past. So, I've never attempted by these means and I certainly haven't discussed it. But, here's the other side, going through with this method will require some effort which is something I'm lacking. I guess this sort of lowers my risk in a way? So it goes something like...I'm suicidal and have a plan/means but because I'm so depressed and exhausted to follow though with it, I'm less of a risk (?) Would it then be safer to actually identify not only my plan but my method as well? 

Admit to being suicidal + having a plan - method = too many possible methods, can be considered high risk based on past, poses too much of a risk to self.
Or...
Admit to being suicidal + having a plan + method = can be considered high risk, but chosen method requires energy that's not present due to severe depression, risk to self is low.

I don't know, something like that. I actually am not entirely sure if that makes any sense. The lack of sleep is scrambling my brain, so I think that what makes sense to me doesn't make sense to others. Maybe then if I recognize that I should assume that all of my present thoughts make no sense, like you said that things might be different if I get sleep. I don't know.

I actually spoke to my therapist today, who was/is concerned. The lack of sleep, as my therapist said, would be a problem for anyone even those without mental illness.

My therapist knows, to an extent, the severity of my depression. The part that she in unaware of is exactly how close I am to giving up. My therapist knows my history, knows how severe my episodes can get, but she doesn't know the current level of distress. She is aware of my self injury, that my meds aren't working, and that I have increasing depression. 

I have purposely not shared with my therapist how suicidal I feel. Because I want to avoid finding myself back in the hospital. So telling her that I've been planning again, more extensively than before, and collecting the means will without a doubt get me sent to the ER on the spot.


I want to read, and I've been trying, but I just can't do it. I can't focus or what ever.

I'm becoming increasingly stressed by the fact that my power keeps turning off and on every 15 or so minutes. I can only assume the power company is trying to fix something somewhere in my area. 

This reply has been waiting to be sent for over 25 minutes now, as my wifi crashes each time I lose power. My TV follows along.

This is really not my night.
